about: The frame of what the agents do on their own (passation-pro briefs/design-agents-proactifs.md §4, §6 row 3, §7.4, §7.5; Alex 22/11: Q6 A, Q7 A, Q8 A; texts validated 22/11 but those listed in `texts.rules.new`). Every routine (routines.rs), watcher (watchers.rs, connectors.rs) and trigger (triggers.rs) has an owner (the agent that does it, the person it is for), an end, and a place where it answers. A « Oui » to a one-time thing is one time; a repeat asks its own « Oui », its card saying its rhythm and its end. The agent's routines run « vers 8 h » (a stable shift of −10 to +10 min drawn from their id); the person's stay exact. What fails is repaired in its frame or stopped with a word: a card `bip-fix-<id>` « Réparer / Arrêter », no model call before « Réparer ». Additions only: an app 1.0 ignores the new fields and draws the generic Yes / No card it already draws for an unknown `bip-` card. Read by bridge/tests_blackbox/test_task_frame.py and task_frame.rs' tests (the bridge), and by the apps' FixCard and lists (branch task-frame-apps). Alex 24/11 (passation-pro textes-1-1/decisions.md): a watcher's fix card is asked again before it stops (`cards.fix_warned`), one card per agent whose AI doesn't answer (`cards.ai`), no end at a default end without the person (`after.default_end`); their new texts (`texts.<lang>.warn`, `ai_*`) are to be validated by Alex.

fields.where: Each item of GET /v1/autonomous of kind routine, watcher or trigger; the job view of GET /v1/agents/{agent}/routines (and the routine routes' {job}); the `watch` of a connector's detail and of its card (`bip_connector_watch`); GET /v1/triggers' items.
fields.owner: {agent: the agent's id, person: "you" or the shown name of the family member who asked for it (a family agent's routine, routines.rs `by`)}
fields.ends: {kind, at?, count?, text}: kind `date` (at: Unix seconds, its last moment), `count` (count: the runs left), `plan` (it goes with its plan, plans.rs), `once` (a one-time routine; a watcher `once`: it stops once it has told its person), `never` (until the person stops it). `text` in the agent's language (texts.<lang>.ends).
fields.deliver: {kind, title, session_id}: kind `conversation` (a routine made in a conversation: its reports go there; title: that conversation's, in /v1/autonomous only, else null), `boite` (the Boîte of the main conversation, or a watcher's or a trigger's own conversation that the Boîte points at), `silent` (a muted routine: its reports stay on its page). The apps say it with texts.<lang>.deliver. In a routine's job view (GET /v1/agents/{agent}/routines, {job}) it is `deliver_to`: the job's own `deliver` stays Hermes' « local », as an app 1.0 reads it.
fields.approx: true: runs « vers » its time (routines only). The job's schedule keeps the exact time (an app 1.0 shows « 8:00 »); `next_run_at` is the shifted one; `when` (in /v1/autonomous) gains `approx: true` and its French `text` says « vers 8 h ».
fields.failures: the failed runs (routines) or checks (watchers) in a row
fields.plan: the plan it is a moment of (routines; null otherwise); a job had it already, a row of /v1/autonomous gains it
fields.fix: the run id of its card waiting (`bip-fix-<id>`), else null

tools.routine_schedule: `create` and `update` take `until` (a date « 2026-11-30 »: through that day on the routines' clock; or a date-time « 2026-11-30T18:00 »), `repeat` (a number of runs, 2 or more: « 10 fois ») and `approx` (default true for a schedule at a time of day: the routine runs « vers » it; false when the person asked for an exact time). A one-time schedule ignores `until` and `repeat`. An `until` in the past, or before its first run, is refused.
tools.connector_register: `watch` takes `until` (a date or a date-time, as above) and `once` (true: it stops once it has told its person what it waited for: « préviens-moi quand les billets sont en vente »).
tools.default_end: A routine or a watcher its agent makes on its own (not in a turn of the person's own conversation: a routine's, a watcher's, a trigger's, a task's turn, another agent's ask, or outside any turn the bridge follows, as plans.rs; review C8) ends within 90 days: with no end given, 90 days after it is made; an end it gives (a date, or a number of runs that would go past them) is brought back to 90 days at most (review C9); « once » watchers too (R2). 3 days before, a card « Garder 3 mois de plus ? » (Alex Q6 A), asked while it is paused too; a default end never takes a paused one (« Arrêter », its switch, a card unanswered for 7 days: review B1): it waits, 3 days from now each look, and any way back on (the person's resume or switch, a « Oui » to its agent's card, the approval of a change, an accepted resume) gives a passed or near one 3 days (review 2, B1 bis). One the person asked for, in their own conversation (a family member in her own turn too), keeps the end they said, none: `never`.

cards.start: The creation card of a routine its agent made (routines.rs) says its end in its sentence, so an app 1.0 shows it too: texts.<lang>.start, `{end}` only for a `date` or `count` end (none: today's sentence). A routine « vers »: `{when}` says « vers 7 h ».
cards.repeat: An agent's change of a one-time routine into a repeat is its own card (`routine_change`, critical): texts.<lang>.repeat, with its rhythm and its end. Its detail shows « Quand : une seule fois (…) → chaque jour vers 8 h, jusqu'au 30/11 ».
cards.watcher: A watcher's connector card (`bip_connector_schedule`, `bip_connector_watch.text`) says its end after its check: « Vérifie toutes les heures, ne réveille l'agent que si ça change, jusqu'au 30/11 » (none: today's line).

fix.fields: agent, run_id, request_id (<id>), command (« task_fix · <name> »), description (= bip_summary), choices, bip_choices, created_at, session_id (null), bip_summary, bip_detail, bip_fix
fix.bip_summary: texts.<lang>.fix_summary.<task> (the app 1.0's whole card: « Oui » = Réparer, « Non » = Arrêter)
fix.bip_fix: {kind: routine | watcher, ref (its id), name, variant: repair, since (Unix seconds: its first failure in a row), failures, reason (looping | too_long | failed | not_started | timeout | secret | check), title (texts.<lang>.fix_top.<task>), text (texts.<lang>.fix_since + the reason's words), buttons (texts.<lang>.fix_buttons)}
fix.when: Routine: 3 failed runs in a row (the scheduled one's silent retry counts): it is paused and the card asks. Watcher: « en panne » (`[watchers] failures_max`, 4): the card asks instead of the bridge's line, at most once a week (watchers.rs `BROKEN_TOLD_GAP`); its agent still learns it with the person's next message. No model call before « Réparer ».
fix.placed: In the main conversation and the Boîte (card_place.rs, no turn), pushed as a request (`tool_request`: « Une demande attend ton accord », its sealed words texts.<lang>.fix_top.<task>). A routine a family member asked for (routines.rs `by`): her card, in the family conversation's pending cards on her bridge, answered from there (`/family/...` served approvals; the creator's /v1/approve: 403), she is pushed; its repair counted to her, and its agent's proposal after « Réparer » is hers too, told to her bridge, never pushed to the creator (review C7, C7 bis). Critical at every level (approval_level.rs `task_fix`: « Réparer » starts a paid turn).
fix.gone: Answered; the routine resumed or deleted by the person; the watcher working again, approved again, switched off or removed by the person (review C11); 7 days without an answer (below). A run that works while the routine is paused with its card (« Lancer maintenant », its agent's `run`) leaves the card: only the person's answer takes it (review C4).

keep.bip_fix: {kind, ref, name, variant: keep, ends_at (Unix seconds), title (the agent's shown name), text (= bip_summary), buttons (texts.<lang>.keep_buttons.<task>)}
keep.when: 3 days before a default end (tools.default_end), once; never for an end the agent or the person gave. Unanswered at its date (Alex 24/11, B2): asked again once, pushed, its date 14 days later (`after.default_end`).
keep.placed: As the fix card; not pushed the first time; its reminder at the default end is pushed (« Une demande attend ton accord »).

fix_warned.about: A watcher's fix card unanswered for 4 days (Alex 24/11, tf-ligne-panne-veilleur-remplacee: « prévenir avant de l'arrêter »): the same card again with a new <id>, placed and pushed, saying the day it stops with no answer; switched off at that day only (7 days after the first card, 3 days after this one at the earliest).
fix_warned.bip_fix: the fix card's, its `text` ending with ' ' + texts.<lang>.warn, and `stops_at` (Unix seconds)

ai.about: An agent whose AI doesn't answer (its model's server off, out of reach, overloaded: task_frame.rs `ai_silent`, read from Hermes' error of the failed run) has ONE card for its routines stopped by it, not one per routine (Alex 24/11, tf-carte-commune-ia-eteinte B): its routines paused at their 3rd failed run in a row each join it. A family member's routine keeps its own fix card.
ai.bip_summary: texts.<lang>.ai_summary (the app 1.0's whole card: « Oui » = Réessayer, « Non » = Arrêter)
ai.bip_fix: {kind: agent_ai, ref (the agent), name (its shown name), variant: ai, since, routines (their names), failures, reason: ai, title (texts.<lang>.ai_top), text (texts.<lang>.ai_since), buttons (texts.<lang>.ai_buttons), after (texts.<lang>.ai_after: what the card says once answered, `once` then `deny`; an app reading no `after` keeps its own words)}
ai.answers: « Réessayer » (once): its routines on again, their count from zero, no model turn. « Arrêter » (deny): they stay paused on their page. Never gone after 7 days: it waits (its routines are paused already). A routine turned back on, or deleted, leaves it to the others.

answers.does: « Réparer »: ONE turn of its agent (no turn before), in its conversation (a watcher's own; a routine's: a hidden run conversation, its reply where its reports land), fed with today's failure (a hidden note). It may change something only through the existing cards: routine_schedule `update` / `resume` (`routine_change`: a routine being repaired is proposed back on), connector_update (the connector card). The routine stays paused until the person's « Oui » to that change; the watcher keeps trying, less often. « Réparer » that could not run or said nothing (no conversation, a failed turn, the month's credit, [SILENT]): one line, no model (texts.<lang>.repair_failed.<task>), and the card again (review C5).

answers.choice: deny (or stop, and the other refusals)
answers.does: « Arrêter »: paused, never deleted (a watcher: switched off), on its page.
« Garder »: its end moves 90 days later.
« Le laisser s'arrêter »: it ends as planned.

after.retry: A scheduled run that fails a first time (none failed just before) is tried again, in silence, 15 minutes after its end (review C3 a) with the same words, unless its next run comes first: no Boîte line, no push. Failed again: today's notice (routines.rs `ended_notice`). A retry missed by more than 2 hours (the bridge down) is not run late: today's notice then (C3 b). A pause drops a retry waiting (C3 d); the last run's retry is never dropped by its end (C3 c). The person's « Lancer maintenant » and the agent's `run` are never retried in silence: told at once, as today.
after.end: An end reached: the routine (a `date` end; a `count` end given here, `frame.count`: a job moved from Hermes stays « terminée » as before; a one-time routine too), the watcher (removed) or the trigger goes, its cards with it; never while its last run's retry waits, never at a default end (Alex 24/11, B2: `default_end`). One that ran more than 7 days leaves one Boîte line, not pushed: texts.<lang>.ended.<task>, a count end saying the runs it was given (review C1), a watcher at its date its date (R12). A watcher `once` stops once its agent told its person what they wait for (never the bridge's own line when its turn failed; its wake-up's note says it is « once »): paused on its page, never deleted (review C2), with no end left nor « Garder ? »: its work is done (review 2, N1).
after.no_answer: A routine's fix card waiting 7 days: the card goes, the routine stays paused, one Boîte line, not pushed: texts.<lang>.stopped.routine. A watcher's: asked again after 4 days (`cards.fix_warned`), switched off at the day it said (7 days at the earliest), one Boîte line: texts.<lang>.stopped.watcher. The common card `ai` waits.
after.approx: « vers »: the run at its time shifted by −10 to +10 minutes (whole minutes, stable for the routine: sha256 of its id, plans.rs `approx_shift`). A one-time or an interval schedule is never shifted unless `approx` is given true for a one-time one. Never to the day before nor after: a run at 0:00 shifted back is shifted forward instead (R8).
after.default_end: A default end (what its agent set up on its own) never ends it without its person (Alex 24/11, tf-fin-par-defaut-de-lui-meme B2). « Garder » (keep): 90 days more. « La laisser s'arrêter » (stop): the end becomes the person's, reached at its date. Unanswered at its date: it goes on, the « Garder ? » card asked again once, pushed, its date 14 days later; unanswered again: it goes on « until you stop it » (ends.kind never), the card gone, nothing more pushed.

app_1_0.about: What an app 1.0 (iPhone and Android) already does: no app change. To check on both 1.0 apps with int-1.1 (« apps 1.0 contre le pont 1.1 »).
app_1_0.same: Every key and value it reads today is unchanged (bridge/tests_blackbox/test_task_frame.py compares the JSON of the routines, autonomous, approvals, connectors and triggers routes with the base int-1.1c 938d65f23, the added keys left out), but on purpose: the sentence of an agent's routine card with an end or « vers » (cards.start, cards.repeat), a watcher's card line with an end (cards.watcher), and `next_run_at` of a routine « vers » (shifted).
app_1_0.fix: the generic card: bip_summary, bip_detail under « i », « Oui » (once: Réparer) / « Non » (deny: Arrêter)
app_1_0.approx: a routine « vers 8 h » shows « 8:00 » (its schedule is the exact one)

rules.lang: The agent's language (names.rs `agent_language`); another than these four: English. Dutch: not yet (texts to validate, briefs/status-task-frame.md).
rules.clock: « vers 8 h » / « around 8 AM » / « gegen 8 Uhr » / « hacia las 8 »; with minutes « vers 7 h 30 », « around 7:30 AM », « gegen 7:30 Uhr », « hacia las 7:30 ».
rules.new: Not in the design's §7 as written, to validate by Alex: clock_minutes, ends.never, ends.once.routine, ended.watcher, keep.routine, keep_buttons.routine, fix_since's date form, the reasons, fix_under_i.routine (fr; de/es from the §7.5 notes), fix_summary.routine, stopped.routine, repair_failed (review C5), the year of a day not this year (review C9). Alex 24/11 (to validate): warn, ai_top, ai_since, ai_buttons, ai_under_i, ai_summary. Alex 25/11 (textes-1-1-lot2 tf2-carte-ia-apres B): ai_after (fr; en/de/es to validate).
